lines.trans: Good afternoon. Ah, it is you?
And I want you to go far away.
We cannot go. We are pregnant.
It is our first pregnancy, we are constantly nervous.
So we snapped at you.
If they fire us, who will feed him?
Fine. After all, the child is not at fault.
Thank you so much from me and from my wife.
Let's go, we are forgiven! A talented improvisation, did you see?
Damn, I forgot my bag. Hold on a second.
I am calling my husband! He will shut your restaurant down completely.
Even if all of you there are pregnant!

examples.text: Езжайте к ней сейчас же!
examples.trans: Go to her right now!

examples.text: Ты сейчас за кого переживаешь?
examples.trans: Who are you worrying about right now?

meanings.note: Prefix 'по-' forms perfective verbs or marks a brief/onset action (stem 'годить'). Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'to wait a little (colloquial)'.

related.gloss: to to wait a little (base verb)
not to to wait a little (negated infinitive)

examples.text: Чёрт, я сумку забыла. Сейчас, погоди.
examples.trans: Damn, I forgot my bag. Hold on a second.

examples.text: Погоди, я сейчас.
examples.trans: Wait, I'll be right there.

examples.text: Ну, погоди!
examples.trans: Just you wait!

meanings.note: Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'am calling', paired with 'позвонить'.

examples.text: Кто звонил? А зачем ты врёшь?
examples.trans: Who called? And why are you lying?

examples.text: Звони ему.
examples.trans: Call him.

examples.text: Кто звонит?
examples.trans: Who's calling?

meanings.note: Common masculine noun meaning 'for your husband' in everyday Russian.

examples.text: Я звоню мужу! Он вообще закроет ваш ресторан.
examples.trans: I am calling my husband! He will shut your restaurant down completely.

examples.text: Что скажет ваш муж, когда увидит в сети запись, где жена сбивает беременную женщину?
examples.trans: What will your husband say when he sees a recording online where his wife hits a pregnant woman?

examples.text: Это мой муж.
examples.trans: This is my husband.

meanings.note: Prefix 'во-' ('into, up') marks inward or upward movement (stem 'обще').

examples.text: Он вообще кроме рыбы ничего не может.
examples.trans: He cannot do anything at all except fish.

examples.text: Я звоню мужу! Он вообще закроет ваш ресторан.
examples.trans: I am calling my husband! He will shut your restaurant down completely.

examples.text: Послушай, я раньше вообще затормозила.
examples.trans: Listen, I braked way before that.

meanings.note: Prefix 'за-' marks beginning an action, covering, or stopping by along the way (stem 'крыть'). Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'will close', paired with 'закрывать'.

examples.text: Здравствуйте. Извините, мы ещё закрыты.
examples.trans: Hello. Excuse me, we are still closed.

examples.text: Мы закроем ваше дело.
examples.trans: We will close your case.

examples.text: Закрой дверь, пожалуйста.
examples.trans: Close the door, please.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian pronominal determiner meaning 'your, yours (polite or plural)', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.text: Ваш салат.
examples.trans: Your salad.

examples.text: Я звоню мужу! Он вообще закроет ваш ресторан.
examples.trans: I am calling my husband! He will shut your restaurant down completely.

examples.text: Что скажет ваш муж, когда увидит в сети запись, где жена сбивает беременную женщину?
examples.trans: What will your husband say when he sees a recording online where his wife hits a pregnant woman?

meanings.note: Borrowed from French 'restaurant' (from 'restaurer', to restore strength with rich broth); entered Russian in the early 19th century.

examples.text: Откуда в ресторане кошка?
examples.trans: Where would a cat in a restaurant come from?

examples.text: Меня зовут Виктория. Я директор этого ресторана.
examples.trans: My name is Viktoria. I am the director of this restaurant.

examples.text: Я звоню мужу! Он вообще закроет ваш ресторан.
examples.trans: I am calling my husband! He will shut your restaurant down completely.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian discourse particle adding conversational nuance meaning 'even', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.text: Даже если вы там все беременны!
examples.trans: Even if all of you there are pregnant!

examples.text: Катя даже собирается к нему домой переехать.
examples.trans: Katya is even planning to move into his home.

examples.text: Лёва! Откуда Лёва? Его даже на кухне не было.
examples.trans: Lyova! Where did Lyova come from? He wasn't even in the kitchen.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian conversational adverb meaning 'there', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.text: Ничего, страшно было? Нет, там такие подушки.
examples.trans: Well, was it scary? No, there are such airbags there.

examples.text: Даже если вы там все беременны!
examples.trans: Even if all of you there are pregnant!

examples.text: Они прямо сейчас там разговаривают.
examples.trans: They are in there talking right now.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian personal or demonstrative pronoun meaning 'all', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.text: Всё нормально.
examples.trans: Everything's fine.

examples.text: Как вы все знаете...
examples.trans: As you all know...

examples.text: Поделись со всеми.
examples.trans: Share with everyone.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian conversational adverb meaning 'already', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.text: Увольнение уже попросил. В этот раз я сама.
examples.trans: You already got us fired. This time I will do it myself.

examples.text: Нас уже простили!
examples.trans: They already forgave us!

examples.text: Помогать не надо, я уже такси вызвала.
examples.trans: No need to help, I already called a taxi.
